research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and OSR sources only; outcome 14-22 definitions, CSEW response/reporting and weighting, police-recorded revision/QA, comparability and governance controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW-police comparable subset
verified_claims: a comparable subset was constructed for offences covered by both measures
more than three-quarters of recent CSEW offences fall into comparable categories
the subset supports adjusted comparison between sources
limitations: the subset is not the full CSEW or full police series
comparison requires the official mapping

sources.name: CSEW offence-code alignment
verified_claims: CSEW offence coding is designed to align closely with police-recorded definitions
alignment supports source comparison
the two sources still use different collection methods
limitations: close alignment is not identity
changes to either coding system require version checks

sources.name: Aggregate public dissemination
verified_claims: ONS crime statistics are released as aggregate data
they are publicly available free of charge
publication uses the Open Government Licence
limitations: aggregate release does not provide confidential record-level data
licensing does not remove statistical limitations

sources.name: Crime release pre-announcement
verified_claims: publication dates are pre-announced
ONS states at least six to eight weeks of notice
the calendar covers planned release timing
limitations: pre-announcement is not a guarantee against justified changes
release date differs from reference period

sources.name: Home Office quarterly QA handoff
verified_claims: the Home Office supplies ONS with a document describing checks and QA for quarterly delivery
the document uses an agreed template
the handoff records the validation performed before ONS compilation
limitations: the QA document is not an independent external audit
its scope must be matched to the delivered edition

sources.name: Post-delivery correction notification
verified_claims: the Home Office must communicate corrections made after data delivery
ONS states this applies regardless of how minor the correction is
the process supports publication revision control
limitations: notification does not mean every prior publication changes materially
minor and major corrections must remain distinguishable

sources.name: ONS editorial responsibility
verified_claims: Home Office analysts quality-assure the draft bulletin
ONS considers their comments
final editorial responsibility remains with ONS
limitations: subject-matter review does not transfer editorial ownership
editorial responsibility is separate from source-data ownership

sources.name: Responsible-statistician sign-off
verified_claims: the responsible statistician signs off the final draft before publication
sign-off follows compilation and quality assurance
the control is part of the official publication process
limitations: sign-off does not make administrative data error-free
later corrections can still be issued

sources.name: Force IT-system variation
verified_claims: crime-data quality is influenced by different IT systems and software versions across forces
some forces can change their systems directly while others depend on suppliers
supplier-dependent changes can be slower and more costly
limitations: system variation must not be converted directly into force performance rankings
the finding is contextual rather than parcel-level

sources.name: 2023 principal-crime-rule change
verified_claims: the 2023 Counting Rules review introduced a single principal crime rule for most offences
modern slavery and passport-application fraud remain exceptions
OSR noted concerns about effects on understanding domestic-abuse offending patterns
limitations: the rule change can create classification discontinuities
the exceptions and domestic-abuse caveat must remain explicit
